relationships.subject: Nanocnide lobata petroleum ether extract
relationships.evidence_quote: Compared with the model group, the petroleum ether extract-treated group showed significant differences in the serum levels of TNF-α (Table 8) and IL-10 (Table 9) on the 7th, 14th, and 21st days.

relationships.subject: Nanocnide lobata petroleum ether extract
relationships.evidence_quote: There was also a significant difference in the content of TGF-β1 in the petroleum ether extract-treated group on the 21st day (Table 10) and in the content of VEGF in the petroleum ether extract-treated group on the 7th and 14th days (Table 11).

relationships.subject: caffeic acid
relationships.evidence_quote: Caffeic acid has been reported to exhibit anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties by inhibiting NF-κB activation and transcriptional activity of the COX-2 gene in epithelial cells

key_findings: Petroleum ether extract of Nanocnide lobata was the most effective fraction for mouse burn/scald healing, altering TNF-alpha, IL-10, TGF-beta1 and VEGF levels.
UPLC-MS identified 39 compounds including ferulic acid, kaempferitrin, caffeic acid and salicylic acid.
